title: Ham or pork with potatoes and cheese sauce

content.title: About
content.content: The dish consists of diced ham or pork, boiled potatoes and a creamy cheese sauce. It is popular in family meals and school cafeterias, combining protein, carbohydrates and dairy.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The cheese sauce is often made from processed cheese, milk and butter.
Ham can be smoked or boiled, which changes the flavor profile.
Potatoes are usually boiled, but can be lightly fried for a crispy crust.
The dish is often baked until a golden cheese crust forms.
In some regions fresh chives or dill are added for brightness.

items.title: Protein source
items.content: Ham or pork provides high‑quality protein needed for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Energy‑dense carbs
items.content: Potatoes supply complex carbohydrates that give lasting satiety.

items.title: Calcium and vitamin D
items.content: The cheese sauce contributes calcium for bone health and vitamin D to aid its absorption.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Meat is rich in B12, B6 and niacin, supporting nervous system function and metabolism.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: Keeping the potato skins adds fiber, which benefits digestion.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Ham often contains a lot of salt, which may be problematic for hypertension.

items.title: Saturated fats
items.content: Cheese sauce and meat can be high in saturated fats, so moderation is advised.

items.title: Dairy allergy or lactose intolerance
items.content: People with these conditions should use alternative sauces.

items.title: Proper meat cooking
items.content: Undercooked pork may harbor harmful bacteria; ensure it is fully cooked.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the dish hot, optionally topped with fresh herbs, sour cream or tomato sauce. It pairs well with a green salad or sauerkraut.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the prepared dish in an airtight container in the refrigerator for 2‑3 days. When frozen, it can be stored up to 1 month after cooling and placing in a freezer‑safe bag.
